figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 1
figures_and_tables_checked.title: High-level view of a multi-LLM system with an adaptive trust metric layer
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Conceptual query → three generic LLMs → trust layer → final decision. No model identities, clinical transitions or execution results.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Table I
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Trust Concerns Across Regulated Industries
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Qualitative industry/risk/trust-need categories, not measured comparative results.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 2
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Evolution of trust mechanisms from rule-based systems to adaptive trust in multi-LLM environments
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Conceptual historical progression; not clinical time or a learned transition experiment.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Table II
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Comparison of Existing Trust Frameworks
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Author assessments of NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC standards and EU AI Act. No systematic assessment protocol or quantitative adoption evidence.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 3
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Layered pipeline for adaptive trust metrics in multi-LLM systems
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Input screening, orchestration, trust engine, governance and output. Supplied visual notes report no explicit adaptive feedback connection in this diagram.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 4
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Comparative weighting of trust dimensions across regulated industries
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Grouped relative-importance chart across five dimensions and four sectors. Sampling, elicitation, empirical units and uncertainty provenance are not reported. Bar-height estimates in prior notes were not independently re-read or promoted to metric results.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Listing 1
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Pseudocode for computing adaptive trust scores in multi-LLM systems
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Fixed weighted sum of unspecified variance, consistency, bias and policy-alignment functions. No executed code path, learned adaptation, calibrated probability or threshold implementation established.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 5
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Healthcare triage flow showing how adaptive trust metrics ensure safe escalation paths for patient queries
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Proposed symptom-query response and clinician-referral workflow. Caption safety wording is an author assertion, not demonstrated safety.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Table III
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Adaptive Trust Outcomes in Healthcare and Finance
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Narrative escalation, explainability, false-positive reduction and audit-trail benefits. No measured outcome, comparator, denominator or uncertainty.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 6
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Distribution of key risks in multi-LLM deployments
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Pie chart displays risk-category percentages without empirical provenance or denominator. Color/category assignments come from supplied visual notes and remain unverified directly.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 7
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Ethical governance cycle integrating adaptive trust metrics into continuous oversight and refinement
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Risk assessment, policy alignment, stakeholder feedback and refinement. A governance cycle is not clinical-state evolution or a measured optimization trajectory.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Table IV
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Open Research Gaps and Future Directions
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Five proposed pathways: scalability, regulatory alignment, cross-domain transfer, human–AI collaboration and evaluation benchmarks.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 8
figures_and_tables_checked.title: Conceptual roadmap of future research layers for adaptive trust in multi-LLM ecosystems
figures_and_tables_checked.review: Conceptual technical-to-societal roadmap. No validated temporal ordering, readiness measurement or causal dependency.
figures_and_tables_checked.inspection_basis: Inherited automated image/text review notes; no new direct visual inspection.

scope_choices: This is an automated API model review and skeptical second-pass synthesis of supplied primary text and prior model-generated page/image notes, not independent human verification or replication.

All eight supplied text pages, including the references, were read. Original page images were not directly supplied to this response; all eight supplied visual-review notes were examined, but their inspection flags are not recast as new direct visual inspection.

Earlier page-review notes contain mutually outdated statements that only pages 1–4 or only pages 5–8 were available. The present input includes the complete text and notes for pages 1–8; those fragment-local availability statements are not retained as current text-access limitations.
The PDF version and SHA-256 are pinned to the supplied source record. The file was not opened, its hash was not recomputed, and arXiv/publisher records were not externally checked.

The abstract claims monitoring implementation and the conclusion claims demonstrated case-study benefits. The described methods comprise a conceptual pipeline, simplified pseudocode and narrative applications; execution and empirical effectiveness are not established.
No named operational LLM configuration, weights, training protocol, dataset, cohort, patient count, split, baseline or empirical result is reported for this framework.

No held-out actual human/clinical evaluation establishes R2. No actual clinician study, prospective shadow use, clinical intervention, comparative effectiveness or authorized monitored release establishes R4–R8.
No learned or hybrid health-world transition, persistent clinical state, future-state prediction experiment, matched treatment comparison or model-coupled planning result is established.

The trust components lack operational measurement definitions, score ranges, normalization, calibration and empirically justified weights or thresholds. The pseudocode has fixed weights and no implemented update mechanism.
The healthcare narrative emphasizes explainability, whereas Listing 1 aggregates uncertainty, consistency, bias and compliance without an explicit explainability term.
Figure 4's relative-importance values and Figure 6's percentages lack reported sampling, elicitation, denominator and uncertainty provenance. They are not entered as empirical MetricResult objects.
The proposed escalation pathway does not establish emergency fallback, clinician response capacity, performance under correlated model errors or improved patient safety.
References [1]–[20] were read as bibliography entries only. Their full texts were not retrieved; cited systems' implementations, human studies and capabilities are not assigned to this framework.
Several bibliography entries have incomplete or nonspecific venue metadata, and some citation-to-claim connections require verification. No alternative bibliographic values were invented.

Regulatory frameworks are mentioned, not shown to be applicable, complied with or grounds for authorization. The paper's wording about a proposed EU AI Act is retained as source wording, not endorsed as a verified legal-status statement.
No new feature assertions are supplied, as requested. Capability and gate assessments therefore do not represent completed 128-feature coverage or an executed feature-criterion validation.
No JSON Schema validator, graph assembler, cross-reference checker or regression suite was executed. Structural and evidentiary checks were manual model checks of the supplied material.
No files, workbook cells, graph artifacts or corpus-progress checkpoints were modified.
